new_entities.name: IV glutathione
new_entities.description: Intravenous glutathione administered for cosmetic, anti-aging, or general wellness purposes.

new_entities.name: Human outcomes
new_entities.description: Overall clinically meaningful outcomes reported in human use, including benefit, harm, or lack of validated efficacy.

edges.effect_quant: The available human literature does not show robust broad-spectrum benefit from IV glutathione. A 2025 dermatology systematic review found that the skin-lightening literature includes only one placebo-controlled IV study, while a 2016 safety review judged IV glutathione evidence inadequate and a 2025 case report described shock-like systemic inflammatory toxicity after an unregulated high-dose infusion.
edges.population: people receiving IV glutathione in cosmetic, anti-aging, or wellness settings
edges.mechanism: Glutathione is an endogenous antioxidant, but moving from biochemical plausibility to clinically meaningful benefit from IV infusion remains poorly demonstrated in human intervention studies.
edges.summary: This is a contested wellness-therapy edge. Human use of IV glutathione is under-studied, the claimed benefits are narrow and weakly evidenced, and case-level safety problems make broad promotional claims inappropriate.
edges.caveats: This edge is not about established hospital uses of glutathione-related pharmacology in highly specific settings. It addresses the consumer-facing IV glutathione infusion claim set, where evidence and regulatory support are both thin.
